qualifying_findings.title: Configuration-driven AI code review gates
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The source frames AI code review as a configurable review layer with rule files, CI or pull-request integration, prioritization of security and logic issues, and measurable review outcomes rather than a generic autocomplete feature.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Local intelligent-code-review guidance can treat AI review as a policy-bearing gate: repository rules, severity filters, review placement, and outcome metrics should be explicit enough for teams to audit.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Company or product coverage belongs upstream; keep only the local review-gate implication.

qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Represent AI code review checks as durable, versioned policy inputs tied to CI or PR gates, with separate handling for security, logic, maintainability, and style findings.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare against docs/wiki/coding-practices/intelligent-code-review.md and docs/wiki/verification-and-evals/code-review-evals-and-rubrics.md for duplicate coverage before adding new language.

qualifying_findings.title: Agentic coding requires bounded human review of generated changes
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Post URL and page date show 2026/08/16.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The author argues that AI-generated code changes shift effort toward reviewing, debugging, and selecting acceptable bug risk, and that higher output volume increases the need for quality gates and reviewer judgment.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki can use this as practice evidence for verification-tax and acceptance-gate guidance: faster code production does not reduce the need for review budgets, reproducible tests, and explicit acceptance thresholds.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Treat generated-code throughput as a review-capacity planning input; require teams to decide acceptable defect risk, test depth, and reviewer ownership before expanding autonomous implementation loops.

qualifying_findings.title: AI coding workflow report emphasizes prompt quality, context, and pull-request review
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The source describes AI-assisted coding speed gains alongside a workflow that depends on clear prompting, contextualizing the task, reviewing generated code, and using normal pull-request practices.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: This is a concise practice signal for keeping prompt packages, context selection, and review evidence in the same operating loop instead of treating code generation as a separate activity.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Keep request packages and pull-request packaging coupled: the agent prompt should name the goal and constraints, while the PR records what was verified and what still needs human judgment.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP remote-tool access raises reviewable capability-boundary requirements
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The MCP digest highlights remote tool integration and cloud-agent connectivity as a current developer concern, including the need to understand which services an agent can reach and how those capabilities are exposed.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Local MCP practice should keep focusing on scoped authorization, tool inventory, approval evidence, and reviewable connector capabilities rather than merely cataloging MCP servers.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Protocol background and server ecosystem coverage belongs upstream.
Company and product coverage belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: For remote MCP-capable agents, capture a capability manifest, resource scopes, approval class, identity context, and audit evidence before enabling write or deployment tools.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, route broad Cloudflare and MCP product facts upstream and keep only capability-boundary practice under docs/wiki/retrieval-and-tools.

qualifying_findings.title: Multi-agent software-development education stresses modular roles and human oversight
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The lesson presents software-development multi-agent architectures as role-specialized systems with planner, coder, tester, reviewer, or manager responsibilities and emphasizes coordination and human oversight.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Local subagent and harness guidance can use the source as practice evidence for explicit role boundaries, handoff artifacts, review loops, and avoiding unowned autonomous work.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Company or course-provider background belongs upstream if needed.
Broad technique coverage belongs upstream; local scope is workflow and oversight practice.

qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Document each subagent's authority, expected artifact, verification responsibility, and handoff criteria instead of only describing a model-to-model chain.

qualifying_findings.title: Language-model coding workflows require source-control and rollback discipline
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Post URL and page date show 2026/Aug/15.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The source collects guidance for using LLMs for code, including working in source control, keeping generated changes reviewable, and relying on tests or other checks rather than accepting output blindly.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: This reinforces local practice pages that make git state, scoped diffs, tests, and rollback paths prerequisites for AI-assisted coding work.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Broad model and technique background belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Before handing coding work to an assistant, require a clean reviewable change boundary, fast verification command, and a rollback path in source control.
